_doc: Walk-the-house checklist, generated from criteria/. Designed for a phone screen while standing in a house. Regenerate when criteria change. Progress is saved per-home in the browser. Tags [Tnn] trace to transcripts/00-index.md.

sections.title: ★ Before you even tour
sections.intro: Two things the videos say to do BEFORE you fall in love with a house, because either one can disqualify it on its own. Both change what you can afford to borrow.

items.text: Get a homeowners insurance quote for THIS SPECIFIC ADDRESS. In wildfire zones this runs $4,500–$8,500/yr in Mountain Shadows and up to $15k elsewhere — $300–600/month on top of the mortgage. [T04][T06]
Pull the FEMA flood map for the address. Monument Creek and Fountain Creek run through our search area. Flood insurance adds $1,000–$5,000/yr and can lower the appraisal. [T04]
Ask whether a metro district applies. It's NOT an HOA, doesn't show up as dues, and adds to the mill levy — Banning Lewis runs $184–229/mo in governance costs before base tax. [T06]
Ask who sends the water bill. All four services on one Colorado Springs Utilities bill = competitive rates. A private water co-op or split providers can add hundreds/month. [T07]
Check the listing price against reality: Q1 2026 average list was $618k but average SOLD was $540k. A $649k listing may be a $570k house. [T05]

sections.title: Foundation & structure
sections.intro: The biggest single risk here. Colorado Springs sits on Pierre shale and bentonite clay that swells up to 20% in volume when wet. Roughly 25% of COS homes have a foundation issue in their lifetime. Give this 10 real minutes.

items.text: Walk the full exterior perimeter. Any stair-step cracks in foundation or brick, especially at corners? [T04]
Drop a marble or a ball on each level. Does it roll? Which direction?
In the basement: cracks in the slab, especially under interior bearing walls? Any heave? [T04]
ASK: Has a structural engineer ever evaluated this home? Is there a soils report? [T04]
ASK: Any repair history — piers, wall anchors, underpinning? A DOCUMENTED, WARRANTIED prior repair is a POSITIVE, not a dealbreaker. Is the warranty transferable? [T04]
Open and close every interior door. Any sticking, or gaps that taper?
Look above every door and window frame for cracks radiating diagonally.
If using FHA or VA: foundation issues are a top reason those loans get killed. Flag anything structural to your lender early. [T04]

sections.title: Wildfire & insurance
sections.intro: Waldo Canyon burned 346 homes in Mountain Shadows in 2012 — that's 6.6 minutes from YWAM, inside our radius. Some carriers have stopped writing new policies in these zones entirely. An uninsurable house is an unbuyable house.

items.text: Do you have the address-specific insurance quote in hand yet? If not, stop and get it. [T04][T07]
Has fire mitigation been done, and is it DOCUMENTED? One house quoted $7,000/yr next door to one at $2,500 purely because they cleared the scrub oak properly. [T07]
ASK: Will your carrier actually write this address, or are you headed to the Colorado FAIR Plan (insurer of last resort — expensive, limited coverage)? [T04]
Under Colorado HB25-1182 (effective January this year) insurers must offer a pathway to premium reductions via mitigation. Ask what specifically would lower the quote. [T04]
How close is continuous vegetation and the foothills interface? Is there defensible space, or shrubs against the siding?
Roof and deck materials — combustible or not? Ember-resistant vents? [T04]
Any trees overhanging the roof? Expect the insurer or lender to require cutting them back — which also helps the foundation. [T04]
How many ways out of the neighborhood?

sections.title: Water, drainage & flood
sections.intro: Nearly every foundation problem here starts as a water problem. At 6,000+ ft, water that gets in during warm months freezes in winter, expands, and creates hidden moisture pockets. Walk the perimeter yourself before the inspection — drainage problems are visible from outside and easy to miss from inside.

items.text: Look for efflorescence on basement walls — white crystalline salt-like deposits. The basement can look bone dry today and this still proves water has been there. [T04]
Does the ground slope AWAY from the house on all four sides? [T04][T08]
Is the house at the bottom of a hill? Be very cautious if so. [T04]
Where do downspouts terminate? One ending 12 inches from the foundation sends every storm straight at the wall. [T04]
Test the sump pump. 30 seconds tells you whether the primary water management tool actually works. [T04]
Is there an interior basement drainage system (tile and channel)? Without one, the risk may not surface until the first heavy rain. [T04]
Crawl space: is there a vapor barrier? Ideally fully encapsulated with sealed walls. [T04]
If in a mapped flood zone — is the house ELEVATED above actual risk? Ask for elevation documentation; it changes the picture completely. [T04]
Any moisture staining or mineral deposits in the basement or crawl space? [T04]
Next to a creek or small body of water? Your insurer may require added flood coverage regardless of the FEMA map. [T03][T06]
Window wells: do they have drains? Any staining showing they've held water?
Is an uphill neighbor's water routed toward this lot? Sprinklers spraying the foundation?
If mold is suspected, book the test NOW — inspection deadlines are legally binding. A $900 drying job becomes $6,000+ if water sits 48 hours. [T04]

sections.title: Roof & hail
sections.intro: Colorado Springs averages 5.5 hail days a year and hail is 60–70% of all Colorado insurance claims. At 6,000+ ft, UV degrades shingles much faster than at sea level. Roofs here are consumables.

items.text: ASK: Roof age, and is there a permit for the replacement? [T04]
ASK: Is your carrier on replacement-cost or ACTUAL CASH VALUE terms for this roof? Carriers are moving to ACV on older roofs — you may not be covered for full replacement. [T04]
Is it Class 4 impact-resistant? That's a 20–30% insurance premium saving, in a place that gets hail every ~5 years. [T04]
NEGOTIATION: don't ask the seller for 'a roof replacement' — ask for a CLASS 4 roof specifically. It saves money every year you own it, not once. [T04]
Check gutters, downspouts, vents, and flashing for hail dents. Soft metal tells the truth even when the shingles look passable. [T04]
Look at the AC condenser fins for hail bruising. [T04]
From the ground, look for more than one shingle layer at the edges — a sign of cheap prior work.
ASK: Any hail claims, paid or denied? Which carrier, and what's the separate wind/hail deductible?
Budget $11,000–$25,000 if it needs replacing. [T04]

sections.title: Systems — the 1970s–80s cluster
sections.intro: Our budget lands squarely in this era. These specific items can make a house uninsurable, and sellers in older established areas are often retired, long-tenured, and unwilling to renovate — assume you inherit the deferred maintenance.

items.text: Open the electrical panel. Brand? Federal Pacific or Zinsco means full replacement.
Aluminum branch wiring? (Stamped ALUMINUM on cable jackets, ~1965–75 builds.) Insurers may refuse or require remediation.
Supply pipe material — gray or blue plastic is polybutylene, often uninsurable.
ASK: Sewer lateral material and age. SCOPE IT REGARDLESS — pre-1980 clay and cast iron fail from root intrusion.
Amp service — 100A at capacity, or 200A?
Furnace and water heater age — read the labels, photograph them.
Water pressure — run an upstairs shower and flush a toilet at the same time.
Kitchen or bath dated? Budget ~$25k for a kitchen, up to $60/sqft for a full remodel — and MORE in older homes because of hidden surprises. [T06]

sections.title: Layout, storage & fit
sections.intro: 4 bed / 3 bath is the hard minimum. This section is about whether it actually works — and storage is the thing Colorado buyers most often regret skipping.

items.text: Count 4 REAL bedrooms. Does any basement bedroom have a proper egress window?
Are all 3 baths usefully placed, or is one stranded?
Storage for outdoor gear — closets, garage, basement. 'You might be in it a year, then realize you have nowhere to put your stuff.' [T08]
Is there a mud room or transition space from outdoors? [T08]
Flex space for cold months and working from home? [T08]
Room to host people?
Would the NEXT buyer find the storage and layout workable? [T08]
Cell signal — check your bars in the basement and back bedrooms.

sections.title: Location, orientation & sun
sections.intro: Drive time is already filtered to 10 minutes. This is about daily life — and sun orientation is the most underrated item in the whole batch. Colorado Springs gets ~300 days of sunshine.

items.text: Which way does the driveway face? SOUTH-facing melts by noon; north-facing means the neighbor is still chipping ice three days later. Worse on a slope. [T07]
Drive the actual route to YWAM at the hour you'd really drive it. Our measured times are free-flow with no traffic — add 15–25%.
Which rooms get afternoon west sun? At 6,000+ ft that's brutal in July. [T07]
Is any deck or patio COVERED? A west-facing deck gives sunset views over Pikes Peak but cooks you at 90° without cover. [T07]
Stand outside and just listen for a minute. Arterial or highway noise?
Mature trees in the neighborhood? You can't fast-forward 30 years of growth, and canopy carries a real premium — but check placement vs. roof and foundation. [T07]
Any trees within ~15 ft of the foundation, overhanging the roof, or dead and unmitigated? Those are liabilities, not assets. [T04][T03]
Mountain views — and could a future build take them?
Backyard privacy and sight lines. Note some west-side areas don't allow 6-ft privacy fences. [T03]

sections.title: Carrying costs & the real monthly payment
sections.intro: The Zillow monthly estimate is almost never accurate. This is where the surprises live — and every item here is knowable before you make an offer.

items.text: ASK: Is there a metro district? NOT an HOA, doesn't show as dues, adds to the mill levy. [T06]
ASK: HOA dues, reserve health, and any pending special assessment. Some homes have TWO HOAs plus a metro district. [T02]
Current property tax and mill levy for THIS EXACT PARCEL. Rates vary widely between zip codes inside the same city limits. [T06]
ASK: 12 months of actual Colorado Springs Utilities bills — a cleaner read on efficiency than any listing claim.
City water/sewer, or well and septic? More likely at the Woodmen Valley edge.
Add it all up: mortgage + tax + insurance quote + HOA + metro district. That's the real number. [T06]

sections.title: Radon
sections.intro: Worth noting: radon came up in NONE of the eight videos. But El Paso County is EPA Zone 1 (highest tier), it's a real health issue, and basements are where bedrooms go. Cheap to fix, so it's a negotiation item rather than a dealbreaker.

items.text: Is there a mitigation system? (Sealed sump, vent pipe, inline fan running to the roof.)
ASK: Has it been tested? What was the number?
If mitigated, ASK for the post-mitigation test result.

sections.title: Offer strategy
sections.intro: We're in a buyer's market: prices fell 5% citywide in 2025, contract fallout is at an all-time high, and the average home sold $79k below the average listing price. Negotiate accordingly.

items.text: Add up what this house actually needs — roof, sewer, radon, drainage — BEFORE deciding the offer. [T04]
Keep a real repair reserve. Target offering $540–570k so there's $25–40k of cushion. [T05]
Model a RATE BUYDOWN vs. a price reduction. A $15,000 buydown often saves more monthly than a $15,000 price cut. [T05]
Ask for seller concessions toward closing costs — commonly $8,000–$10,000 in this market. [T05]
Ask for a Class 4 roof specifically, not a generic roof replacement. [T04]
Does the payment work at TODAY's rate and TODAY's insurance quote? Don't assume appreciation or a future refinance. [T08]
Exit test: if we had to move fast, could we sell and recover? Is the loss acceptable? Could we rent it? [T08]
